doc.title: Joel Dorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007

title: Opening: why record production takes passion and a bit of craziness
summary: Monk Rowe introduces Dorn. Dorn says you need passion for the work and that producing is not regular work, quoting his father's advice to be great at whatever you do.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: My name is Monk Rowe and I’m very pleased to have Joel Dorn with me today for the Jazz Archive at Hamilton College.
It’s great to be here. And I try to paraphrase you fairly closely. You said one time that you have to be pretty crazy to do what I do, or what you do.

Yeah I mean I might have been in a lighthearted moment where I was trying to be semi- profound. I just think you have to have a passion for whatever you do. You know like if it’s, I mean my father used to tell me he said, “if you want to be a barber,” he said, “be a great barber.” He said, “if you want to be a surgeon, be a great surgeon.” He said really do — you know he didn’t do what he loved doing to make a living so he was happy when my brother and I chased a dream, chased passions. I think you’ve got to love it, and crazy comes with it. Because this isn’t regular work. You know, it’s not a job. You don’t have real rules. There are rules but you determine your reality by how you improvise inside of those rules if you want to produce records. So it’s tricky. And I guess it’s not for regular people.
